title: Unique Key
statement: Implement `solve(tags)`. Build a canonical key for a bag of tags: strip, lowercase, drop empties, unique, then sort. Return that key as a list of strings. Two inputs that differ only by order, case, or duplicate tags must return the same list.
constraints: tags is a list of strings
hints: Normalize each tag before you put it in a set.
Sort the unique values so the key does not depend on input order.

approaches.name: Direct
approaches.explanation: A set of tags is the right uniqueness structure and the wrong key, because set order is not part of the value.

editorial: A set of tags is the right uniqueness structure and the wrong key, because set order is not part of the value. Sorting the normalized unique tags makes a canonical list. Callers can compare those lists, or tuple them, and treat the bags as equal.
